text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- State security police arrest and interrogate 10 people suspected of involvement in an attempt against the life of leading pro-democracy MP Abdullah al-Naibari on Friday. Naibari's condition is said to be stable.

- U.N. compensations fund to receive $600 million for Gulf War victims from limited Iraqi oil sales renewed by the U.N. Security Council earlier this month. Under a deal with the United Nations, Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of oil to buy food over a six-month-span.

- Qatar's Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani visited Kuwait's Crown Prince and Prime Minister Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah on Saturday in Britain. Since he underwent a colon operation in March, Sheikh Saad has been abroad for further medical checks and recuperation.
- Moroccan products fair to be hosted in Kuwait in October.
- Finance Minister Nasser al-Rodhan says proceeds from corporate tax imposed on foreign companies operating in Kuwait reached 173 million dinars ($573 million) since 1985.
- Coast guard on Thursday arrested 30 Iranian infiltrators in Kuwaiti territorial waters.
- Experts laud Kuwait on safeguarding environment.
